title: finite étale scheme torsor lifting
statement: Let i:Y₀ → Y be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] inducing an equivalence on finite étale schemes [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category]. Let M be a finite abelian group and R₀ a torsor under the constant abelian sheaf M on Y₀_et [def-sc-gm-torsor, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then there exist a scheme M-torsor t₀ over Y₀, an isomorphism of its sheaf torsor with R₀, a scheme M-torsor t over Y, and an isomorphism e:P ×_Y Y₀ ≅ P₀ over Y₀ commuting with every M-action map. A scheme M-torsor means a finite étale surjective scheme with an M-action whose map ∐_M P → P ×_Y P is an isomorphism [lem-galois-etale-torsor-sheaf-torsor]. No connectedness, nonemptiness or surjectivity of i is assumed. The conclusion concerns geometric representatives and their actions only; no sheaf inverse-image comparison, unit equations, or arbitrary torsor transport is asserted.

proof.text: Generalize the sorry-free constructions in EtaleTorsorDescent as private proof helpers, without importing its cyclic HenselianFiniteEtale dependency. A local section identifies the underlying torsor sheaf with the constant sheaf by translation. On a geometric stalk every germ is a translate of a fixed local section; after restricting to a fibre of the locally constant translating coefficient it is a translate by an element of M. Thus the underlying sheaf is locally constant with finite geometric stalks. Apply finiteLocallyConstant_sets_representable. Transport the M-action across the representing isomorphism. Yoneda gives the action equations; local sections give surjectivity. The Yoneda map of the simple-transitivity morphism is bijective: freeness follows by evaluating coefficient functions at points, and a pair of sections is locally related by a unique coefficient function, whose open fibres glue a morphism to the coproduct. This produces t₀ and its sheaf-torsor equivalence with R₀. Cancellation on sections uses Mathlib concrete iso laws and naturality uses NatTrans.naturality_apply. The coefficient-to-stalk surjection works without finiteness; finiteness is imposed only when deducing finite stalks. Coproduct decomposition allows varying summands, and local triviality applies to any constant group sheaf. The private action laws and equivariance are checked directly in the constructed torsor.

In the finite étale category form X₀ from t₀. Essential surjectivity provides X and eX:F(X)≅X₀. Define each action morphism on X as the full preimage of eX.hom ≫ a₀(m) ≫ eX.inv. Apply faithfulness to its zero and addition equations, after mapping them and cancelling eX.inv ≫ eX.hom. Forgetting to schemes gives the action, the base-change isomorphism e, and their equivariance equation.

Construct the coproduct of copies of X in the finite étale category using the scheme coproduct, and its binary product using the scheme fibre product. Verify the universal properties explicitly by Sigma.desc and pullback.lift. The equivalence F preserves these colimit and limit cones. The unique comparison isomorphisms identify the image of the simple-transitivity morphism with the corresponding morphism formed on F(X). After conjugating by e on each coproduct summand and both fibre-product factors, that morphism is the invertible one of t₀. Check this equality on every summand and both projections. Reflect its invertibility through F and forget to schemes.

Let U be the open image of the finite étale structure morphism π. Étaleness makes the image open and finiteness makes it closed. Its open immersion j:U→Y is also a closed immersion, hence finite étale. The pullback range formula and the surjectivity of t₀ show that the base change of j is surjective, hence an isomorphism. View j as a morphism of finite étale objects from U to Y, and reflect the isomorphism of its pullback through F. Its range is therefore Y; since U was the image of π, π is surjective. Package these proofs and the lifted action equations into t and supply e and its compatibility equations.
